objectives.statement: Explain the constitutional function of the Government in directing domestic and foreign policy, civil and military administration, and defence of the State.
Identify the constitutional members of the Government and distinguish the optional presence of Vice-Presidents.
Distinguish the President's direction and coordination powers from the individual responsibility of Ministers.
Identify the constitutional incompatibility rule applicable to members of the Government.
Explain how the President of the Government is appointed and how the other Government members are appointed and removed.
Apply the constitutional rule that Government members are jointly responsible for its political action before Congress.
Distinguish ordinary judicial responsibility from the special criminal-responsibility rules for the President and Ministers.
Identify the constitutional instruments through which the Government may initiate legislation and issue delegated legislative provisions.
Explain the parliamentary mechanisms of questions and interpellations addressed to the Government.
Identify the constitutional conditions for a motion of censure and its constructive-censure requirement.
Distinguish the question of confidence from a motion of censure as mechanisms of parliamentary confidence.
Explain the constitutional limits on dissolution of the Cortes Generales by the President of the Government.
Identify the territorial entities whose autonomy the Constitution guarantees.
Explain the constitutional status of the municipality as the basic local entity and its governing arrangements.
Relate the province to the grouping of municipalities and identify the constitutional guarantee of provincial autonomy.
Apply the constitutional requirement that local entities have sufficient means to perform their functions.
Identify the matters that an autonomy statute must contain under the Constitution.
Distinguish the residual, exclusive and state-framework dimensions of the constitutional distribution of competences.
Identify the constitutional controls applicable to acts and provisions of Autonomous Communities.
Explain the constitutional exceptional measure available to the Government when an Autonomous Community seriously fails its obligations.
